summary:
Two parts, both in src/finder/mod.rs, with one line in inline_rename.rs and the scope bar's own listener removed from bars.rs (54 lines added, 17 removed in src).

1. The net. `Finder::keyboard_lost` is registered with `cx.on_focus_lost(window, ..)` in `Finder::new`, beside the window-activation observer. GPUI calls it when the frame before drew what has the keyboard and this one does not. When the nearest thing still drawn around what went (`window.focus_lost_restore_target`) is this browser's own handle or anything inside it, and no name is being edited, the files get the keyboard, and `window.defer(cx, |window, _| window.refresh())` asks for the frame that draws them as focused (a focus moved inside a focus-lost listener asks for none). Hidden tabs and split view's other pane are told too and do nothing: the nearest drawn thing is not inside them.

2. The press. `Finder::keyboard_stays` is an `on_any_mouse_down` listener on the browser's root div. It runs where the root's own focus-on-press ran, for a press nothing inside claimed, and takes its place: the keyboard stays where it is in this browser, or goes to the files when the root itself has it or it is outside this browser, and the default is prevented so the root never takes it. A press whose default was already prevented (a part that took the keyboard, a kit button) is left alone.

3. src/finder/bars.rs: the scope bar's mouse-down listener from scope-chips-keep-focus is gone. The root's listener does the same for every bar.

4. src/finder/inline_rename.rs, `keyboard_back`: after a rename in the sidebar's tree the files get the keyboard when the tree is no longer showing (`show_sidebar && tree_on()` false).

The plan of record wanted a strict match (`restore target == this.focus`). The code acts for any target inside the browser, with a guard for a name being edited. I checked that choice instead of undoing it: with strict equality three kept tests fail (a file's menu after Cmd+1, the Back button's menu after Cmd+Alt+S, F2 then Back), and so does the test added in review for a button under No Results that goes with the keyboard on it.
changelog: The keyboard no longer goes dead when the part of the window that has it goes away. With the sidebar as a folder tree, a click on a row gives the tree the keyboard, and hiding the sidebar then, or switching it to a list, left every key doing nothing until something was clicked: not even Cmd+Alt+S brought the sidebar back. The same happened when a menu's item or button went from under it, as after Cmd+1 with a file's right-click menu open, and when Back or another shortcut left the folder while a name was being edited. The files now get the keyboard. A click on something that takes no keys doesn't take the keyboard away either. After a click on a row of the sidebar's list, the path bar, the status bar, or the empty part of a bar, the arrow keys and typing did nothing until a file or a field was clicked. The keyboard now stays where it was, in the files or in the search field, and a right-click or middle-click there leaves it alone too. In split view, such a click in the pane that doesn't have the keyboard gives it to that pane's files.
behaviour_changes: Tree sidebar: with the keyboard in the tree (a row was clicked), hiding the sidebar with Cmd+Alt+S or the Hide Sidebar button, switching it to a list, or the same setting changed from another tab or window, gives the keyboard to the files. Before, no key worked until a click, and Cmd+Alt+S could not show the sidebar again. Tested, and pictured.
Split view: only the pane whose tree went takes the keyboard, with both panes drawn. Tested in review, both ways round.

A menu that stops being drawn while it has the keyboard gives it to the files: a file's right-click menu then Cmd+1; the Back or Forward menu then Cmd+Alt+S in a window about 900 pt wide. Both tested. By the same code, any context menu whose row or button moves or goes.
F2 on an item, then Back or another shortcut that leaves the folder: the files get the keyboard. The name stays as it was, as before (location_changed drops the edit). Tested.

A rename in the tree when the sidebar is hidden or shown as a list: what was typed is kept, as before, and the keyboard goes to the files instead of to a tree that is not there. With the window in the background the edit waits: it resumes if the tree comes back, and ends in the files when the window is active again without the tree. Tested, all three.

A button that has the keyboard and goes gives it to the files: Hide Sidebar pressed with Space after Tab (probed by the implementer and again in review), and a button under No Results that a right-click gave the keyboard, when the search finds something without it (tested in review).

A press with any mouse button on what takes no keys no longer takes the keyboard: rows of the sidebar's list (Recents, Favorites, Locations, Trash, Smart Folders), the sidebar's blank parts and its edge, the toolbar's empty space, the path bar and its crumbs, the status bar, the blank parts of the other bars, a disabled button (the sidebar's blank part and edge, the toolbar's title and a disabled Forward button probed in review). Before, the keyboard went to the browser as a whole: shortcuts worked, arrows and typing did not. On macOS the toolbar's empty space is where the window is dragged by, so moving the window took the arrow keys away (from reading window_drag_area; not run on macOS).

So after a click on a favorite, a Smart Folder or a path crumb the arrow keys, type-to-select, Return, Space and Delete act on the files at once, and their selection stays drawn as active (tested for a favorite, a Smart Folder, the status bar and the path bar's blank part; a crumb probed in review; pictured in light and dark).

With the keyboard in the search field it stays there: typing goes on after a click on the status bar (tested), and a click on a favorite ends the search and the next letters start another in that folder (tested). Down Arrow in the field then moves into the files (probed in review). The filter field and the Nushell panel's field keep it the same way (the Nushell field probed in review).
In tree mode the tree keeps the keyboard after a click on the status bar (tested). A click in the tree gives it the keyboard as before.

A click outside the files during a rename: the edit ends at the press with the name kept, as before, and the files then have the keyboard, where before nothing did. A row of the sidebar's list also goes to its folder, with the name kept first. A refused name goes on being edited. Tested in review. In the tree the keyboard goes back to the tree (probed).

A menu closed by a click on the chrome gives the keyboard back to where it was before the menu (the files, the tree, a field). Before, the root took it at the press and the menu had nothing to give back. Probed in review for a file's menu, the toolbar's Sort menu with the keyboard in the files and in the tree, and the search field's own menu.

The mouse's Back and Forward buttons no longer take the keyboard either (probed in review: Back on the status bar goes back with the keyboard still in the files, or in the search field; during a rename the name is kept first, as with any press outside the field).
Split view: such a press in the pane that does not have the keyboard gives it to that pane's files. Before, it went to that pane as a whole. Tested.
With the keyboard in the filter field, a click on a Smart Folder that has no filter closes the bar and the files get the keyboard. Tested.

Scope bar: its chips, the funnel and (i) behave as before, and a right or middle press on the bar now leaves the keyboard alone too. One change in split view: a press on a button of the other pane's scope bar (Save, (i)) no longer brings the keyboard to that pane at the press, since no button does. With the keyboard in the first pane's files the end is the same as before, because the dialog's opener gives that pane's files the keyboard. With it in a field of the first pane, the dialog now gives it back to that field when it is cancelled.

A button that has the keyboard (reached with Tab, or given it by a right-click, which the kit does) keeps it through a click on the chrome, like everything else in the browser. Before, such a click left the keyboard nowhere. Probed in review: Return then presses the button.
File chooser: the same code. After a click on a bar's blank part Return and Escape act on the files, and Escape there cancels the choice. Not probed.

Unchanged: a left click on any button, menus that close in the usual ways, dialogs (they are drawn outside the browser; probed in review with their animations on), a click on a tab (its files get the keyboard), Quick Look's own window.

Manual: Keyboard shortcuts starts with a paragraph on which part of the window has the keyboard and what a click on the chrome does; the Folder tree bullet says that hiding the sidebar or switching it to list mode gives the keyboard to the files.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
No Workspace-level fallback, as the plan of record said. Tabs and split view give the keyboard to the files themselves when they change (focus_active).

A right or middle press on an enabled kit button still gives that button the keyboard, where Return and Space press it. The kit's button takes it before the browser's root looks, and the root leaves alone whatever took the keyboard at a press: it cannot tell a button from a part that should take it without knowing what had the keyboard before.

A context menu whose button moved from under it stays open as far as the kit knows after the files took its keyboard. It shows again, without the keyboard, when the button is back under the pressed point, and a click closes it (probed in review with the Back menu and Cmd+Alt+S twice at 900 pt: Down Arrow then moves in the files under the menu, and Escape does not close it). A menu whose row is gone for good does not come back (probed: a file's menu, Cmd+1, Cmd+2). See Found, not fixed.

After a rescue the keyboard always goes to the files, also when what was lost sat inside a tree that is still drawn (a tree row's vanished menu, a tree rename dropped by a key that leaves the folder) or was a field's own right-click menu.
When a shortcut leaves the folder during a rename the typed name is still dropped, as before. Only the keyboard is rescued.
Quick Look's own window has no net of its own: the listener is registered on the browser's window.

No kept test for the file chooser, for the Hide Sidebar button pressed with Space, for a menu closed by a click on the chrome, or for a Return that waits for results through a click on the status bar. The middle two were probed in review.
Nothing was compiled or run for macOS or Windows. The change has no cfg-specific code and changes no signature.
cargo clippy --features term was not run: src/term is untouched and nothing it calls changed. tests/term_mode.rs is in the default build and passes.
README.md and the Search Syntax dialog are unchanged: neither states anything this affects.
No pictures of the menu and rename cases: shot.sh cannot click IDs made of a name and a number. The tests cover them.

review_fixes: Added tests/folder_tree.rs the_files_of_the_pane_whose_tree_went_get_the_keyboard. The implementer kept no test for a focus loss with two browsers drawn, only for a hidden tab. The two differ: a hidden tab is not drawn at all, so a net that asked only 'am I drawn?' would pass the tab test and still hand the keyboard to the wrong pane. I made that mutation (`self.focus.contains(&self.files_focus, window)` in place of the nearest drawn thing) and ran tests/folder_tree.rs: this is the only test there that fails with it. It hides the first pane's sidebar with the keyboard in its tree, then the other pane's, and expects the files of the pane that lost its tree to have the keyboard, the other pane to have got no key, and Down Arrow to select there. Seen failing without the change.

Added tests/basics.rs a_click_outside_the_files_ends_a_rename_and_gives_them_the_keyboard. This is the one place where 'the keyboard stays where it is' would be wrong: the name's field must not go on taking keys after a click on the status bar, and the typed name must not be lost when a favorite's row takes the window elsewhere. It works because the field ends its own edit in the capture phase of the same press (on_mouse_down_out in inline_rename.rs), before the root's listener looks. Nothing pinned that for the root's listener. The test covers the status bar, a favorite's row (name kept, then its folder shown), and a refused name, which goes on being edited with the keyboard in its field. Seen failing without the change at the first files_focused.

Added tests/controls.rs a_button_under_no_results_that_goes_by_itself_leaves_the_files_the_keyboard. The empty-state-messages record handed this case to this brief and the implementer's tests did not cover it: a right-click gives the button under No Results the keyboard, the toolbar's Search Only in button then widens the search, and the button goes with the keyboard on it. The files get it. It also pins the wide match with something that is neither a menu nor a name's field. Seen failing without the change.

Rebased onto 5624239 (typo-fallback-near-miss), which landed after the implementer's commit and touches only crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs and the manual's search text. No conflicts. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the rebased commit.
Nothing in src or in the manual was changed in review. I looked for a reason to and did not find one; the doubts that remain are under notes.
notes:
Checked. With the commit's src diff reverse-applied, 17 of the 19 new tests fail, each at an assertion about where the keyboard is; the two 'goes on while in another app' tests pass, as guards should, and so do the two existing tests whose setup changed. Eight of the implementer's mutations of the final code, one at a time, run against the implementer's sixteen tests and the two existing ones whose setup changed, each failed the tests it should and no others: no deferred refresh (the drawn-with-the-keyboard test); no rename guard (the two guards); no check of which browser lost it (the other-tab test); strict equality (the two menu tests and F2 then Back, and, run separately, the button test added in review); keyboard_back without its two conditions (the two tree rename tests); no default_prevented return (the other pane's status bar test); always the files (the tree, the sidebar list and the typing tests); no prevent_default (seven tests). A ninth of my own, 'any browser that is drawn' in place of the nearest drawn thing, run against tests/folder_tree.rs, fails only the split view test added in review. The implementer's mutations of keyboard_back's two conditions one at a time, and of the two clauses in keyboard_stays one at a time, I did not run again. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit: 711 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The 41 tests of the three binaries that have keyboard, rename, keys_work or typing_goes_on in their names pass with SEED=0, 1, 7, 42, 99 and 1234. I looked at the window myself: after a click on the status bar the selected row is still drawn in the active colour, in light and in dark, where the before pictures show it grey; and with the sidebar as a tree, a click on Recents and Cmd+Alt+S twice ends with the sidebar back, which the second press could not do before.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the probes say. (1) The files take the keyboard from something that should have kept it. The net acts whenever the frame before drew the keyboard inside this browser and this frame draws it nowhere, whatever holds it now, so anything that is given the keyboard a frame before it is drawn would lose it. I went through everything that moves the keyboard. Dialogs are drawn in the kit's own layer after the app's content, outside the browser in the dispatch tree (probed: the browser's handle does not contain the keyboard while Settings is open), and the kit's blur while a dialog animates out has a restore target in that layer or none, so the net stays out (probed with reduce_motion off: the keyboard comes back to the files, to the search field, and to the files when the tree it came from was put away under the dialog, since focus_before_dialog moves it to the files first). A toolbar menu is given the keyboard while the frame that draws it is being rendered; a context menu in a deferred callback before that frame, and is drawn in it unless its button is no longer under the pressed point, in which case it would not show at all. Tabs and split view focus the files of a browser that the same frame draws. The search field is drawn at every window width (probed down to 260 pt). A name's field is the one thing that must get the keyboard back by itself when it is drawn again, and the guard and two tests cover it. (2) A press that used to end something no longer does. keyboard_stays runs exactly where the root's focus-on-press ran: same hit test, same phase, after everything inside the browser and before everything outside it, and it prevents the default as that did, so nothing above the browser sees a different press. What changes is only where the keyboard ends up. A rename is ended by its own capture-phase listener, not by losing the keyboard (tested in review). Nothing listens for the search or filter field losing the keyboard. (3) The wrong browser takes the keyboard. FocusHandle::contains reads the frame just drawn, and focus_lost_restore_target only names handles in it, so a hidden tab's handle can match nothing; with two panes drawn the nearest drawn thing is inside one of them only (tests for both).

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) After a click on a favorite with the caret in the search field, the caret stays in the field, as the orchestrator's note asked ('unless a text field had it'). Letters typed next start a search in that folder instead of selecting by name, and a Smart Folder's words can be typed over. Finder gives the files the keyboard on any click in its sidebar. If a click that goes somewhere should do that here, the rows' click listeners in sidebar.rs (or navigate) are the place, and the third part of a_click_in_the_sidebars_list_leaves_the_keyboard_where_it_was turns around. (b) A button that has the keyboard keeps it through a click on the chrome, so after Tab in the files (one press reaches Hide Sidebar) or a right-click on a toolbar button, a click on a favorite and then Space or Return presses that button, where before they did nothing. The ring on the button shows where the keyboard is, and a click on a file takes it. I tried the rule 'the files take it unless the files, the tree or a field has it' on paper and left it: a toolbar menu is closed by a click on the chrome only after the press has gone round, so that rule would send the keyboard to the files where the menu now gives it back to the tree or the field it came from. (c) The menu left open in the kit after its button moved (left_out). (d) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows. (e) Two tests lean on things outside this change: the history-menu test on a 900 by 600 window in which hiding the sidebar re-fits the toolbar, and the drawn-with-the-keyboard test on the test platform drawing a changed window at the end of an update.

For briefs still to come.
- split-active-pane: a press on a pane's chrome now puts the keyboard in that pane's files (not in the pane's own handle) unless it was already somewhere in that pane, so `contains_focused` on a pane's handle still tells which pane is active. No click focuses `Finder.focus` itself any more; only code does. A button never moves the keyboard between panes, the scope bar's buttons included (they did until now, through the bar's own listener): a_click_on_the_other_panes_status_bar_takes_the_keyboard_to_its_files pins that through the Nushell panel's Run, and Finder::keyboard_stays is the one place to change it (its default_prevented return). Tab from the files still lands on Hide Sidebar after one press, and a click on the chrome no longer takes the keyboard off that button (doubt b). In split view ("fav", ix) and status-text repeat in both panes: use click_in("split-pane", ..) for the other pane, and keep one sidebar hidden to click the first pane's rows by ID, as the_files_of_the_pane_whose_tree_went_get_the_keyboard does.
- inactive-selection-colour: after a click on the chrome the files keep the keyboard, so the selection stays in the active colour; the pictures here show it for the list. The net asks for one more frame after it gives the files the keyboard, so views that read files_focused(window) while drawing are drawn again with it. If you add that read to the icon and gallery views they are covered the same way.
- split-view-toolbar-clip: the_keys_work_on_when_a_history_menu_is_left_behind_by_its_button needs a window (900 by 600) in which Cmd+Alt+S moves the Back button from under the pressed point. If your fold or the sidebar's new cap changes that, it fails at '!ui.menu_open()' with the message 'in a window this wide, hiding the sidebar moves Back': pick another width, or another way to move the button, and keep the rest.
- path-bar-no-io: tests/controls.rs has one more caller of `fffinder_core::places::breadcrumbs(&fx.dir)`, in a_click_on_the_status_bar_or_the_path_bar_leaves_the_keyboard_in_the_files, which counts the crumbs to click to the right of the last one. Give it the new argument with the others.
- collapsible-sidebar-sections: a press on a heading is a press on what takes no keys, so in list mode the keyboard stays where it is and the heading needs no handling of its own. In tree mode the whole scroll area tracks the tree's handle, so the press gives the tree the keyboard, as a press on a row does. Collapsing a section does not undraw the tree's handle, so nothing is lost.
- regex-content-search, recent-searches, tab-bar-overflow, tab-drop-and-close, and anything else that adds a control to a bar or the sidebar: the scope bar no longer has a listener of its own; the browser's root has it for every bar. A plain element needs nothing: its press leaves the keyboard where it was. A kit Button refuses the keyboard on a left press by itself. A popover trigger stops the press, and its menu gives the keyboard back to where it was. A text field takes the keyboard before the root looks. A control that is drawn only sometimes can go with the keyboard on it (after Tab or a right-click); the net then gives the files the keyboard, so no hand-off of your own is needed.
- context-menus-fit: the_keys_work_on_when_an_items_menu_loses_its_item right-clicks a file's row in the list view and expects a menu; it does not read the menu's items.
- stale-rows-on-place-change: the_file_keys_come_back_when_a_key_leaves_the_folder_during_a_rename expects Back during F2 to end with the files focused, 'Projects' selected and Down Arrow moving on. location_changed still drops the name being typed (Found, not fixed); if you make it keep the name, the test's 'nothing was renamed' line turns around.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: the_keys_work_on_when_an_items_menu_loses_its_item goes list, Cmd+1, Cmd+2 and expects Down Arrow to select Projects, the row after the one that was right-clicked, which holds if the selection is kept through both switches as it is today.
- tree-arrows-past-smart-folder: keyboard_back in inline_rename.rs now gives the files the keyboard after a tree rename when the tree is not showing; the tree's keys are untouched. a_click_on_the_status_bar_leaves_the_keyboard_in_the_tree presses Right in the tree after the click and expects the favorite to open.
- type-select-space: after a click on the status bar the files keep the keyboard, and a_click_on_the_status_bar_or_the_path_bar_leaves_the_keyboard_in_the_files types 'ro' there and expects Roadmap.md selected.
- idle-redraw-after-search: the net asks for exactly one frame, once, each time it gives the files the keyboard (window.defer then window.refresh). It is not a source of repeated draws.
- quick-look-empty-state: in term mode Quick Look's dialog is drawn outside the browser, so the net stays out when its focus handle is not drawn (the early `return dialog`); the keyboard is then on a handle nothing draws, as before.
- restore-session-tabs: every Finder registers one focus-lost listener on its window when it is made; nothing to do for tabs made at launch.
- stray-double-click-opens-file, collapsed-groups-empty-view, column-pane-selection-by-path, icon-tile-hit-target, go-to-folder-keyboard, preview-page-keys: independent. A press inside the file area is claimed by the files before the root's listener looks, and a press stopped in the capture phase never reaches it. In `Render for Finder` the root div has one more line, `.on_any_mouse_down(cx.listener(Self::keyboard_stays))`, after the two mouse-button handlers for Back and Forward.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change).
- location_changed drops a name being edited without ending the edit: a shortcut that leaves the folder during F2 (Back is tested; any other goes the same way) loses what was typed, where a click on a favorite keeps it and every other way the field goes keeps it too. The manual's Rename row does not say so. The keyboard is rescued now; the name is not.
- The kit keeps a context menu open after its button moved from under the pressed point, and shows it again, without the keyboard, when the button is back there. Reached before this change by Cmd+\ twice with a history menu open (history-menus record); now also by Cmd+Alt+S twice in a window about 900 pt wide. Only a click closes it: Escape goes to the files. Each menu's builder could close it for itself, as history_menu does when the window changes size, or the kit could.
- A right or middle press on an enabled kit Button gives it the keyboard and a ring, and Return and Space then press it. Seen on a view button in the toolbar and on the buttons under No Results.
- Quick Look's own window: nothing there gives the keyboard back when a button that has it goes (the Explore and Text buttons are drawn only for files that can be explored). From reading quick_look.rs; not run.
